create_discussion params: title*, body*, category, integrity, secrecy.

For a rule with 100+ importing/call-site files, the productive strategy is: read the rule's OWN helper functions for internal asymmetries first, THEN grep the corpus only for the specific shapes that asymmetry predicts.

A rule's own .test.ts file is authoritative for whether a behavior is a known/intended limitation vs an undiscovered bug - always check the test file before filing an issue about a suspected gap. Read what the test's EXAMPLE actually represents, not just its valid/invalid label - a test covering one shape (e.g. incidental-metacharacter prose strings) does not cover a disjoint shape (e.g. deliberately-authored fragment constants).

Issues auto-expire (~1wk TTL) and get bot-closed as not_planned - a single expiry is NOT reliably 'unfixed housekeeping': multiple confirmed instances of a fix landing in the same window as expiry. ALWAYS re-read the current rule source before deciding to refile an expired item.

Bash sandbox flags multi-command chains, xargs, sort, printf-with-newlines, some grep -E patterns, and for-loops with variable expansion as 'contains expansion'/'multiple operations requiring approval' even with zero actual shell variables - prefer the Grep/Glob/Read tools over Bash for exploratory searching; reserve Bash for single simple gh/git one-liners. Grep tool also rejects lookaround (?<!...) - PCRE2 not supported, use plain character-class negation instead.
